l.i: traque in suæ matris domum: rependat
vobis Iova pietatem, qua tum erga mor-
tuos, tum erga me usæ estis. Faxit
Iova ut quietem suum utraque apud ma-
ritum nanciscamini[?]. Hæc cùm locuta, e-
as deoscularetur, illa in lachrymas erum-
pentes, affirmabant, sese cum ipsa ad ejus
populares esse reversuras. Sed Noemis e-
as ita hortata est: Revertimini meæ filio-
læ, cur me comitemini? Nunquid ego ad-
huc in utero gesto filios, qui vobis futuri
sint viri? Revertimini meæ filiolæ, disce-
dite: nam ego quidè grandior sum, quàm
ut sim apta viro. Quod si maximè spem
esse putarem, virōq; vel in proximam
noctem tradita, filios gignerem, an estis
expectatura, donec adoleverint, & tam
diu sine viris duratura? Non ita, meæ
filiæ. Equidem valde vestra causa doleo,
sed me Iova manus urget. Tum illa plo-
ratum integrant, & Orphasocrum suam
osculata, ei valedicit. At Rutha cum ea
harebat, &c. Ruth.I.
LXXIII.
Interea dum apud socrum manet, Noe-
mis cum ea sic locuta est: Requiem tibi,

page.notes: The text reads "Orphafocrum", which is most likely "Orpha socrum" with the long s set as f and the space missing; I have written "Orphasocrum" with plain s, and the printed spacing is uncertain. "Rutha" is printed as such (the book's spelling of Ruth's name). The line "nancisc amini" may hold a printed line-end hyphen that is not clear on the scan, hence the [?]. The bare numeral at the middle of the page is rendered "LXXIII." as read from the spaced letters, which may actually be LXXIIII. A small stray dot in the left margin beside "popularés" is a blot or stain, not a marginal note, and is left out. The final word "mea" stands alone at the lower right and is recorded as the catchword. No marginal notes are printed on this page.
